name: Siege of Agrigentum
intro: Agrigentum (Akragas), the great Greek city on the south coast of Sicily, 262 BC, early in the First Punic War. Carthage holds it with a strong garrison. You are the consuls Lucius Postumius Megellus and Quintus Mamilius Vitulus, with four legions.
debrief: In Polybius’s account, the Romans built two camps and siege lines and endured sallies by the garrison. After five months Hanno came with a relief army and took the Roman supply base, so that besiegers and besieged both went hungry. Roman horse drew the Numidians into a trap, and after two more months Hanno gave battle and was beaten when his mercenaries broke back into his own elephants. The garrison under Hannibal Gisco escaped by night across the Roman lines; the city was taken and its people enslaved. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: Rome has its first great city in Sicily.
lose: The legions starve in their lines.

decisions.title: The siege of Agrigentum
decisions.text: Carthage holds the great Sicilian city of Agrigentum with a strong garrison under Hannibal Gisco. You are the consuls Lucius Postumius and Quintus Mamilius, with four legions.

hint.text: The garrison is large and the city well stocked.

scout.text: Ring it with two camps and lines of ditches, and starve it.

choices.label: Build two camps and siege lines around it

fx.text: Two camps and a double line of ditches close the city in.

choices.label: Storm the walls at once while the garrison is unready

fx.text: The garrison sallies against your foragers.

decisions.title: Foragers attacked
decisions.text: Your foragers are scattered across the fields. The garrison sallies out against them and against your camp.

hint.text: Discipline wins this kind of fight.

scout.text: Keep the guards at the camp and the foragers under cover.

choices.label: Keep the guards firm; call the foragers in

fx.text: The guards stand. The sally is driven back with heavy loss.

choices.label: Send everyone out to chase the raiders
Abandon the outer foraging grounds to keep the men safe

decisions.title: Hanno comes
decisions.text: After five months, Carthage sends Hanno with a relief army, cavalry and elephants. He takes your supply base at Herbessus. Now you are the hungry ones.

scout.text: Draw his Numidians onto your own horse, who can fall back on the camp.

choices.label: Lure the Numidians onto your horse and the camp

fx.text: Your horsemen feign flight; the Numidians follow onto the camp and are cut up.

choices.label: Attack Hanno’s army at once, before it settles

fx.text: A hard fight, with no result.

choices.label: Give up the siege and fall back

decisions.title: The battle
decisions.text: After two months, Hanno offers battle. Hannibal signals from the city that his men are starving.

hint.text: The Carthaginians fight with mercenaries in front and elephants behind.

scout.text: When the mercenaries give, they will fall back on the elephants and throw everything into disorder.

choices.label: Accept battle and break the mercenaries

fx.text: The mercenaries break and fall back on the elephants. The whole Carthaginian army is thrown into disorder.

choices.label: Keep inside the lines and let him attack you

fx.text: Hanno tests your lines and pulls back.

choices.label: Split the army to face both him and the town

decisions.title: The garrison escapes
decisions.text: In the confusion, Hannibal leads his garrison out at night across your lines, filling the ditches with baskets of straw.

hint.text: Your men are celebrating the victory.

scout.text: Keep the guard on the lines tonight of all nights.

choices.label: Let them go and take the city in the morning

fx.text: The garrison escapes. In the morning you take the city and sell 25,000 people into slavery.

choices.label: Double the guard and cut off the breakout

fx.text: The garrison is caught in the ditches and taken.

choices.label: Storm the city at once in the dark

fx.text: Fighting in the dark streets costs many men.
